messages:
priya_csm: Weekly account health check for Kepler — p95/p99 split by route/model and streaming vs non-stream. Quick summary: p95 up ~12% W/ W, p99 up ~20%. Biggest regressions on /generate-chat with redwood-75b-qa when streaming enabled. Full snapshot below.

priya_csm: ```
Route | Model | Mode | p95(ms) | p99(ms)
generate-chat | redwood-75b-qa | streaming | 320 | 650
generate-chat | redwood-75b-qa | non-stream | 210 | 480
summarize | opt-6.7 | streaming | 180 | 400
summarize | opt-6.7 | non-stream | 150 | 300
embed | embedding-2 | n/a | 90 | 160
```

amanda_cs_ops: :eyes: Is the traffic pattern different this week or did we change any rollout flags?

priya_csm: Traffic +8% overall (longer prefixes from Kepler mobile), but the skew is 70% of tail from a small subset of users doing multi-turn sessions. No flags toggled in customer config on our side.

mike_infra: Checking infra metrics — KV cache hit rate for redwood-75b-qa dropped to ~48% from 72% around 2026-03-17 21:00 UTC. Memory pressure visible on nodes serving streaming sessions. Also saw a couple of kernel fallbacks in the runtime logs (GPU->CPU path) around same window.

lina_sre: No SLO alerts fired (error rate steady at 0.4%), but streaming request queue depth did climb briefly to 14 on a couple of hosts. Nothing that triggered the pager yet.

kevin_runtime: Noted. The kernel fallback could explain p99 spikes on streaming — streaming keeps the KV cache hot longer and we might be triggering eviction + kernel selection that is slower. Quick mitigations: bump stream-worker mem to avoid thrash, and pin redwood-75b-qa streaming traffic to nodes with the new cu-opt kernels. We can also try a 10% canary of quantized variant for streaming to compare.

priya_csm: Action items: 1) mike_infra — increase streaming worker mem on kepler pool and monitor KV hit rate (ETA today EOD). 2) kevin_runtime — schedule 10% canary of quantized redwood-75b-qa for streaming (start tomorrow morning). 3) amanda_cs_ops/lina_sre — coordinate a customer sync if tail persists; include sample trace set.

amanda_cs_ops: I'll draft the customer note; recommend framing as "investigating tail with targeted infra and runtime adjustments" and include expected timeline.

mike_infra: Started hoisting mem on 3 nodes (kepler-pool). Quick command for trace pull I used: ```bash
./infra-tool fetch-traces --customer kepler --since 2026-03-17 --route /generate-chat --tail-only > kepler_traces.tar.gz
```

deploy-bot: deploy  -> canary-quantized-redwood-75b-qa scheduled at 2026-03-19T09:15:00Z on kepler-pool (id: canary-231).

kevin_runtime: After canary runs, I'll post a simple comparison table (p95/p99 streaming vs non-stream for canary vs baseline). If canary reduces p99 by >15% with similar quality, propose rolling to 50%.

priya_csm: Renewal risk note: health score still green but tail spikes are customer-visible. If p99 persists >600ms on /generate-chat for next week we'll escalate to exec sync. For now risk low but watch closely.

lina_sre: I'll add an SLO watch rule to fire if p99 > 600ms for >30m on kepler-prod routes.

amanda_cs_ops: Thanks — I'll send the customer note after deploy confirmation. :thumbsup:

priya_csm: Thanks team. Follow-ups: mike (update kv hit rate in thread when done), kevin (post canary numbers), amanda (customer note).

mike_infra: kv hit rate back to ~70% on the hoisted nodes after 40m. Early improvement on p95 for streaming: ~300 -> 280ms. Will monitor. :white_check_mark:

kevin_runtime: Canary started, collecting 2h window. Will post numbers when finished.

priya_csm: Great — will reconvene if we see any regressions. If no, we'll keep customer updated tomorrow. :calendar:
